t.7.62.1: When Lavaṇa had been slain, the gods, together with Indra and led by Agni, spoke these very sweet words to Śatrughna, the scorcher of foes.
t.7.62.2: By good fortune the victory is yours, dear child, and by good fortune the rākṣasa Lavaṇa has been slain, O tiger among men! Choose a boon, O Rāghava.
t.7.62.4: Having heard the words of the gods, the heroic, mighty-armed Śatrughna, self-possessed and composed, with hands joined in reverence upon his head, replied.
t.7.62.3: O mighty-armed one, all of us who have assembled here are bestowers of boons, wishing victory for you, for the sight of us is never in vain.
t.7.62.5: May I swiftly obtain a dwelling in this delightful Madhupurī, charming and fashioned by the gods; let this be the boon I have chosen.
t.7.62.6: The gods, their minds delighted, said to Rāghava, "So be it! The delightful city of Śūrasenā shall come to be, there is no doubt."
t.7.62.7: Having spoken thus, those great-souled ones then ascended to heaven. Śatrughna too, of great splendor, brought up that army.
t.7.62.8: Having heard Śatrughna's command, that army came swiftly; and Śatrughna, by his order, began the setting up of the encampment.
t.7.62.9: In the twelfth year that auspicious city, resembling a divine one, was settled, and the realm of the Śūrasenas became free from fear from any quarter.
t.7.62.10: The fields are laden with crops, and Vāsava sends rain in due season; the city, free from sickness and peopled with heroic men, is protected by the arms of Śatrughna.
t.7.62.11: Shaped like a half-moon, it was adorned by the banks of the Yamunā, adorned with splendid mansions, and adorned with squares and markets.
t.7.62.12: And that great desolation which Lavaṇa had formerly wrought, the hero made beautiful with an abundance of manifold wares.
t.7.62.13: Śatrughna, the younger brother of Bharata, his purpose accomplished, beheld that prosperous city and, supremely pleased, attained the highest joy.
t.7.62.14: Having settled the lovely city of Madhurā, the thought arose in him: “In the auspicious twelfth year, I should behold the feet of Rāma.”
